evidence: The paper states "For all cases, permutation tests confirmed (p-values < 0.001) that the probability that the model was obtained by chance is quite low," but these are model-level significance tests, not feature importance inference. The paper compares fingerprint-based random forest model performance (via BACC, AUC, R²) against descriptor-based approaches (Figure 3) without analyzing feature-level impurity importance. Fingerprints range from 79 to 4860 bits with mixed types, and the paper concludes that "PUBCHEM, MACCS and ECFP/FCFP encodings were found to yield the best results for most properties" based on model performance comparison, not feature importance ranking.
